vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: akm-fitness-planner
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a structured set of AI prompts and templates for a fitness planning assistant called 'AKM Fitness.' It focuses on a 'profile-first' approach, instructing the agent to elicit specific user constraints such as injuries, equipment availability, and time budgets before generating workout plans. There is no executable code, no evidence of data exfiltration, and no malicious prompt injection intended to subvert the agent's behavior for harmful purposes. All files, including SKILL.md and the various prompt templates, are strictly aligned with the stated goal of providing constraint-aware fitness advice.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only, profile-first fitness planner that does not request credentials or system access and its required files and prompts are coherent with the described purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (constraint-aware fitness planner) matches the actual content: a three-stage elicitation → record → execution method. It does not request unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths. One minor inconsistency: the registry lists the Source as "unknown" but SKILL.md points to a public GitHub repo (https://github.com/sirsws/akm); this is likely a metadata gap rather than a functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are limited to reading the included prompt and template files and eliciting user-provided fitness state (goals, injuries, equipment, time, recovery). That scope is appropriate for the stated purpose. The skill explicitly forbids giving medical diagnoses and requires surfacing MissingInputs rather than fabricating information. It does require collecting potentially sensitive personal health information from users (injuries, pain, recovery), which is expected for a fitness decision aid but should be treated as sensitive by operators.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry (the skill is instruction-only), which is low risk. SKILL.md includes example install instructions using 'npx skills add' pointing at a GitHub repository; this is a reasonable suggestion but means users who run that command should inspect the upstream repo. Because the registry package itself contains only markdown and no executable code, there is no direct install-time code execution risk from the registry listing alone.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, binaries, or config paths. The prompts do request personal health and habit data from the user (appropriate for the purpose) but do not ask for system or cloud credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not ask to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Model invocation is allowed (default) which is normal for skills and appropriate here. There is no indication the skill tries to persist credentials or alter platform configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it is an instruction-only fitness decision workflow that asks the user for goals, injuries, equipment, time budget, and recovery state. No credentials or system access are requested. Before installing or running the suggested 'npx skills add' command, review the upstream GitHub repository referenced in SKILL.md (https://github.com/sirsws/akm) yourself so you can confirm there is no unexpected code. Treat any health-related answers as sensitive personal data — do not provide identifiable medical records or private identifiers. Do not use this skill as a replacement for professional medical or rehabilitation advice; the skill itself explicitly states that boundary.
